cards.definition: A large section of the Earth's crust and upper mantle that moves slowly over the mantle below.
The edge where two tectonic plates meet; the location of most earthquakes and volcanoes.
Where two plates move apart, allowing magma to rise and form new crust, e.g. Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
Where two plates converge and one is forced beneath the other (subduction), often causing earthquakes and volcanoes.
Where two plates slide past each other horizontally, causing earthquakes but no volcanic activity.
The process where a denser oceanic plate is forced beneath a less dense continental plate into the mantle.
The point inside the Earth where an earthquake originates.
The point on the Earth's surface directly above the focus of an earthquake.
A logarithmic scale used to measure the magnitude (energy released) of an earthquake.
Vibrations that travel outward from the focus of an earthquake through the Earth's crust.
